question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it start as community/experimental support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: Current main and the latest release deliberately validate and document macOS, Linux, and Windows paths, while FreeBSD support would add an ongoing package, service, docs, CI, release, and owner commitment.

options.title: Start as experimental FreeBSD support
options.body: Use the existing FreeBSD ports package as a community path, document caveats, and only promote to Tier 1 after OpenClaw-owned installer, service, and release-smoke proof exists.

options.title: Sponsor Tier 1 FreeBSD support
options.body: Accept ongoing maintainer ownership and split the work into tracked tasks for ports coordination, installers, rc service management, docs, CI, and release validation.

options.title: Keep FreeBSD community-maintained
options.body: Leave FreeBSD packaging outside the official support matrix and document that policy instead of advertising OpenClaw-owned FreeBSD support.

recommendation.title: Start as experimental FreeBSD support
recommendation.body: Use the existing FreeBSD ports package as a community path, document caveats, and only promote to Tier 1 after OpenClaw-owned installer, service, and release-smoke proof exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a support-tier and release-ownership decision crossing product scope, docs, installers, and official platform validation.
